description: Frozen mandatory case list for the P0 systematic acceptance round. Cases G* = guard/network (pure local). Cases P* = perprocess/lifecycle. Cases M* = matrix/evidence. Cases I* = integration (real backend short smoke, after safety gate). The original 24 items keep their frozen semantics from systematic-closure-20260929-01; new tests this round are numbered N01+. No case may be removed after freezing and expectations must not change. exit_code in result.json = the script's own planned exit; the outer runner (matrix/harness) records the actual observed exit separately and both must agree in the mapping.

cases.description: Normal guard interception: sync connect to non-routable is rejected by guard, with matching BLOCKED log entry for THIS run
Guard missing: no PDF2ZH_GUARD_LOG env -> fallback catches all attempts -> test FAILS (guard absent)
Partial guard failure: guard loaded but one hook (e.g. async) disabled -> fallback catches async attempt -> test FAILS
Guard log unwritable: guard loads but cannot write GUARD_ACTIVE/append -> startup gate blocks entry
Stale handshake: GUARD_ACTIVE from old run (different PID) -> startup gate rejects
Sync connect rejection: guard blocks sync socket.connect
Async connect rejection: guard blocks asyncio create_connection (Proactor)
httpx request rejection: guard blocks httpx AsyncClient request
DNS rejection: guard blocks getaddrinfo for non-loopback
Controlled loopback success: real temp loopback listener accepts connection; guard allows loopback
Inherited proxy not used: child env has proxy set but guard still blocks direct (no tunnel)
Empty hostname NOT treated as loopback (tightened _is_loopback)
Fallback counter: normal guard run -> fallback hit count = 0 (guard worked, fallback untouched)
Startup gate: guard handshake verified BEFORE app import in child bootstrap (not in finally)
Startup gate: guard fails to load -> child bootstrap exits before any app code runs
Proxy env save/restore: all proxy vars correctly saved and restored (existed/value structure, case-insensitive dedup, try/finally)
Perprocess short run: 2+ valid samples, full exit code, owned PID/creation-time recovery evidence, port release
Perprocess result: structured result.json with exit_code, samples, guard status, process identities, port release, processes_recovered from identity recheck
Evidence check: all mandatory paths exist, hashes match, no gitignore leakage; checker executed for real with recorded exit
Index accuracy: INDEX links to actual files, no fabricated paths
Baseline short smoke: startup, API, root page, preview, idle, recovery (no translation)
Attribution normal import: full handshake, valid measurement, recovery evidence
Attribution import-fail: all payloads fail, exit non-zero, processes reaped
Matrix regression: all mandatory cases on current code version pass with reason assertions

new_cases_this_round.description: Pseudo-loopback rejected by BOTH layers: 127.audit.invalid / localhost.audit.invalid / empty host / malformed IP never reach real resolution or connect
Entry-gate mutation self-tests: corrupted guard_test copies (partial-sync-also-bad, no_guard wrong exit, deleted subitem, fake timeout) are each rejected by the wrapper
Evidence checker mutation self-test: 13 bad-copy variants each rejected with precise reason; clean copy passes
Perprocess failure-path result: injected exception still yields a structured result with planned vs outer exit recorded

notes.exit_code_semantics: result.json exit_code is the entry script's planned exit decided after cleanup. The matrix/outer runner records the actually observed process exit code; the mapping in REQUIREMENTS.json records both. This documents the schema distinction required by the authorization prompt without changing the frozen expectations.
notes.two_pass_protocol: M01/M02 are self-referential: their evidence IS the final recorded checker execution, which cannot precede itself. Protocol: a prior green checker execution (runs/checker-final-pass1.json with status PASS and recorded exit) is used to derive the M01/M02 coverage rows; the final binding run then validates the complete tree INCLUDING those rows. While the rows are absent, the checker exempts M01/M02 from in-tree coverage counting (documented exemption, printed in its output).
notes.historical_evidence: All prior-round runs remain historical snapshots under their own roots and are NOT counted in this round's mandatory statistics unless re-executed on current code.
notes.reuse_accepted: C1 asset check core, C3 PNG PIL decode, case-6 reason assertion, F1/F5 contract v1.2, sealed PDFs+logs are retained cores; retained cores do not exempt their surrounding isolation/recovery from this round's checks.
